title: Module 8: Test with Automated Test Framework (ATF)
description: The software testing lifecycle and ServiceNow's built-in testing options: the Test Management application, the Automated Test Framework (ATF), and the Script Debugger.

questions.prompt: What is the Automated Test Framework (ATF) used for?

choices.text: Creating and running automated tests inside a ServiceNow instance
Managing manual user acceptance testing on a Test Board
Monitoring production performance and system uptime metrics
Migrating application code and update sets between two separate ServiceNow instances

questions.explanation: ATF is a built-in application for creating and running automated tests within a ServiceNow instance, used for regression testing, test-driven development, and confirming the instance still works after a change.

questions.prompt: By default, the system property that allows tests and test suites to run is set how, and why?

choices.text: Enabled, so that newly created tests run automatically on every instance
Disabled, so that tests are not accidentally run on a production system
Enabled, but only for users holding the script_debugger role
Disabled, because ATF requires a separate license to be purchased first

questions.explanation: The property to run tests/test suites is disabled (false) by default to prevent tests from accidentally running on production. It should be enabled only on sub-production instances, since running tests can cause data corruption and outages.

questions.prompt: On which type of instance should ATF tests be run?

choices.text: Only on the production instance, after a change is live
On any instance, since ATF never modifies real data
On development, test, and other non-production instances
Only on instances that have the Test Management plugin active

questions.explanation: Tests should be run only on development, test, and other non-production instances. Running them on production risks data corruption and outages, which is why the run property defaults to disabled.

questions.prompt: What does ATF do with the data created while a test runs?

choices.text: It tracks the data and rolls it back after the test completes
It commits the data permanently to the target tables
It exports the data to an attachment for manual review
It copies the data into a separate archive instance

questions.explanation: ATF tracks the data created by running tests and rolls those changes back after testing. Even records you modify during the same session while a test runs are rolled back when the test completes.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the Automated Test Framework are correct? (Choose 3)

choices.text: It is upgrade safe and keeps working after platform upgrades
It does not require a separate license purchase
It supports tests with no scripting as well as scripted tests
It can only test server-side logic, never client-side forms

questions.explanation: ATF is part of the platform, so it is upgrade safe and needs no separate license, and tests can be built with no scripting or with scripting. It tests both client-side (forms via the Test Runner) and server-side behavior.

questions.prompt: The Test Management application is primarily a tool for what?

choices.text: Automatically executing scheduled regression tests in the background overnight
Debugging synchronous server-side business rule scripts
Managing the phases of the manual software testing process
Importing test data from external spreadsheets into tables

questions.explanation: Test Management streamlines the management of the manual testing process, providing a repository for tests, test cases, and test suites and supporting test execution, environments, and plans. ATF is the tool for automated testing.

questions.prompt: In Test Management terminology, what is a test suite?

choices.text: A repository that holds a group of test cases
A single condition checked during execution
The instance where testing will take place
The tasks describing how a feature is to be tested

questions.explanation: A test suite is a repository of test cases. A test case is a collection of related tests, a test is a collection of conditions/steps, the test environment is the instance, and a test plan describes how testing is done.

questions.prompt: In Test Management, how is a test case defined?

choices.text: A collection of several related individual tests
A repository that stores many test suites
An instance designated for running the tests
A single step that submits a form to the server

questions.explanation: A test case is a collection of related tests. Test cases are themselves grouped into a test suite (a repository of test cases).

questions.prompt: Which role is required to use the Script Debugger?

choices.text: atf_test_designer
tm_test_manager
script_debugger
admin only, with no specific debugging role

questions.explanation: The Script Debugger is available to users with the script_debugger role. The atf_test roles are for ATF, and the tm_ roles are for Test Management.

questions.prompt: What is the Script Debugger primarily used for?

choices.text: Validating that client-side UI policies hide the correct fields
Debugging Business Rules and other synchronous server-side scripts
Recording browser actions in order to generate automated UI test steps for ATF
Rolling back records that were changed during a failed test run

questions.explanation: The Script Debugger is the primary strategy for debugging Business Rules and other synchronous server-side scripts. It can pause any server-side script running in an interactive transaction, such as script includes, script actions, or UI actions.

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects the modern view of software testing in the testing lifecycle?

choices.text: Testing is a single line-item task performed once the product is fully built
Testing is a series of activities included before and during development
Testing should be performed by the developers who wrote the code
Testing only matters for applications that integrate with outside systems

questions.explanation: The software testing lifecycle is a methodical series of activities, increasingly included before and during development rather than only at the end, to maximize quality and catch regressions early.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the software testing lifecycle (STLC) phases?

choices.text: Test planning, Requirement analysis, Environment setup, Test case development, Test execution, Test cycle closure
Requirement analysis, Test planning, Test case development, Environment setup, Test execution, Test cycle closure
Requirement analysis, Environment setup, Test planning, Test execution, Test case development, Test cycle closure
Test case development, Requirement analysis, Test planning, Environment setup, Test cycle closure, Test execution

questions.explanation: The STLC phases run in this order: requirement analysis, test planning, test case development, environment setup, test execution, and finally test cycle closure.

questions.prompt: Which of these ATF test steps can be configured without any scripting?

choices.text: Performing a JavaScript unit test against server logic
Running a custom test script with an output assertion
Opening a new form and setting field values on it
Asserting on the body of a previously parsed REST response

questions.explanation: Steps such as Impersonate, Open a new form, Set field values, Validate field values, and Submit the form require no scripting. Unit tests, test scripts, and server-side asserts are the scripted/server-side examples.

questions.prompt: How is the output of an ATF test step referenced in a later step?

choices.text: Through a variable, using a syntax that resembles an Angular expression
Through the ${field_name} dollar-sign-and-brace substitution syntax
By calling gs.getProperty() with the prior step's name as the key
By dot-walking from the current object as in a server-side script

questions.explanation: Each step's output is available in a variable, and the reference syntax looks more like an Angular expression than the ${ } substitution syntax used elsewhere in the platform. No JavaScript is required, though it can be added.

questions.prompt: Which capability does the ATF Test Runner provide?

choices.text: Multi-browser testing of client-side test steps
Automatic correction of defects found in the code
Permanent storage of all records created by a test
Scheduling of business rules to run on a calendar

questions.explanation: The Test Runner enables multi-browser testing of the client-side steps in a test; tests with client-side steps open in a separate Client Test Runner window.

questions.prompt: Which roles are associated with the Automated Test Framework? (Choose 2)

choices.text: atf_test_admin
atf_test_designer
tm_test_manager
script_debugger

questions.explanation: ATF uses the atf_test_admin and atf_test_designer roles. The tm_ roles belong to Test Management, and script_debugger belongs to the Script Debugger.
